text:
meera: heads-up — customer ACME reported a sudden p95/p99 tail latency jump after the model-ingest + tokenizer tweak we deployed last night. impact concentrated on very long sessions (>30k tokens).

jonathan: any sample traces or reproducible payloads?

meera: pasted the support log: 
```
request_id=acme-98321 path=/v1/generate model=alto-v1 tokens=48000 latency_ms=1250 p99_backend=1870
worker=worker-12 kvcache_miss=0.87 queue_ms=210
```
They say normal p99 was ~300ms before. This started after the "wordpiece-merge" change.

li: quick note — the new wordpiece merge can expand some multibyte sequences into 3–5x more subwords for CJK + emoji-heavy inputs. That will blow up KV cache pressure and increase batching variance.

kelsey: can we repro locally? meera: yes — steps below (minimal):
```bash
# repro (use long prompt with mixed emoji/unicode segments)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"alto-v1","input":"'"$(python3 - <<PY
print("🍣"*8000 + "中文"*2000 + " the quick brown fox"*1000)
PY)"'"}'
```
Run that a few times, measure p95/p99. On my devbox p99 increased from ~420ms to ~1600ms after the tokenizer change.

jonathan: thanks. can you also grab a kernel trace (cpu/gpu) and the kvcache eviction counters? we need to confirm whether the dominant cost is tokenization or cache backend thrashing.

meera: attached snippet from profiling on a reproduce run:
```
[profiling] tokenization_ms=320 kvcache_lookup_ms=920 self_attention_ms=50 overhead_ms=30
kvcache_evictions=1200 kvcache_size=1.2GB
```
So most time is in kvcache lookup/evictions, not attention.

li: that aligns with expansion hypothesis. mitigation options: 1) temporary rollback of wordpiece-merge flag 2) increase per-worker kvcache cap + pre-warm for long sessions 3) enable token condensation step (coalesce rare-subword runs) as a short patch.

kelsey: what's lowest-risk fast action?

jonathan: roll back flag for model=alto-v1 in prod canary, run a small ramp and check p95/p99. I can push the rollback and set a 30-min watch. Also add a config to temporarily pin older tokenizer version for the model.

meera: will open a support update to ACME to say we're investigating and will attempt a rollback in next 20m.

triage-bot: incident created: INC-3850123456 — "alto-v1 tokenizer expansion causing KV cache thrash and p99 tail spike" assigned to eng-runtime.

jonathan: I initiated the rollback canary for 10% of traffic to alto-v1 at 3850123500. If p99 drops we proceed with 100% within 15m.

meera: can confirm: canary p99 dropped from ~1.8s to ~360ms, queue_ms down. I'm pushing customer update now. :thumbsup:

kelsey: follow-ups: (a) add unit tests that generate emoji/CJK long sequences and compare token counts across tokenizer variants, (b) add kvcache eviction alert threshold tied to model tokenizer diffs, (c) plan a permanent fix for condensation or incremental merge that preserves token count for long-contexts.

li: also recommend a short-term autoscale knob to increase kvcache memory for affected workers so customers with long sessions don't see a hard spike while we ship a fix.

meera: noted. assigning RW-issue-1129 to eng-runtime for root cause and RW-issue-1130 to devex for tests. I'll update ACME with the rollback progress and ETA for permanent fix.

jonathan: great work triage team — we'll keep this thread as the action log.

meera: closing the active rollback phase; will update with RCA summary once eng-runtime finishes root-cause.
